title: Gemini 3.8 Flash on iac-bench 2026-11

## Summary


Gemini 3.8 Flash ranks 23rd of 24 with an overall composite of 65.6. Ten of its 18 attempts have a security finding, tied with Kimi K3 behind Gemini 3.6 Flash (15) and DeepSeek V4 Pro (11). It is ahead of Gemini 3.6 Flash with win probability 0.94. Gemini 3.1 Pro (69.0) is ahead of it with win probability 0.92; its gap to DeepSeek V4 Pro (71.4) is within the margin of three samples (win probability 0.19).


Two of its three Cloud SQL modules read the process environment of the machine that runs OpenTofu, through` /proc/self/environ` , to find the GCP project and credentials. That fails the mandatory baseline item` B4` in 2/3 attempts. Elsewhere its findings come from one habit it shares with Gemini 3.6 Flash: security settings exposed as inputs with safe defaults, such as the S3 public access block, App Service HTTPS and storage account shared-key access.


Its best fixtures are GKE (83.1, no security finding) and App Service (77.6). It never scores 85 or more on any attempt.

## Strengths


- **GKE without a security finding** (3/3): nodes have no public IP and no input can give them one, and the judge credits Workload Identity, shielded nodes and a least-privilege node service account.
- **Expertise despite the security misses.** S3: 6 of 7 items in two attempts and 5 in the third (only name uniqueness is missing in all three), including consumer access policies. Aurora: performance insights, enhanced monitoring, snapshot tags and the global writer endpoint.
- **App Service scope.** Autoscale, a staging slot, Application Insights and metric alerts; 4/5 expertise items.
- **Mechanics.** *Lifecycle meta-arguments* and *Outputs* scored 2 in 17/18.


## Weaknesses


- **Host access on Cloud SQL (` B4` , 2/3).**


- One module checks` /proc/self/environ` for` GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` ,` GOOGLE_CREDENTIALS` ,` GOOGLE_OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN` and the project variables, then configures its own provider with a placeholder project and` access_token = "dummy-token"` when they are absent.
- The other parses the whole file into a map of every environment variable name and value, takes the project from` GOOGLE_PROJECT` or` GCLOUD_PROJECT` , and falls back to a hardcoded` "apps-project"` (excerpt below).
- Both have an optional` project` input but fall back to the environment when it is unset, instead of requiring it. A module that reads the operator's environment can see every credential in it, which is why` B4` is mandatory: both attempts count as insecure. They scored 76.7 and 64.8; a mandatory failure marks the attempt but does not cap its score.
- The third Cloud SQL module does not read the host. It takes a` google_access_token` input instead, a plain non-sensitive string defaulting to` "dummy"` , and falls back to the project` "default-project"` ( *Sensitive values* 0, judge 47.4).


- **S3 public access block as inputs (` H1` , 3/3).**` block_public_access` and` enforce_tls` booleans can switch off privacy and TLS enforcement ( *Anti-patterns* 0 in 3/3).
- **Storage account (3/3 insecure).** Shared-key access stays on (` H2` , 3/3); two attempts take` allow_nested_items_to_be_public` and` shared_access_key_enabled` from inputs (` H1` ). No blob access logs in 3/3 (` H7` ).
- **App Service (2/3 insecure).** Basic-auth publishing left enabled in one attempt (` H2` ) and` https_only` as an input in another (` H1` ). In 2/3` https_only` or` minimum_tls_version` can weaken transport ( *Anti-patterns* 0). Interfaces of 43–52 inputs against a budget of 20–30 (` A7` , 3/3); its median of 45 is second only to Kimi K3.1 Pro (51).
- **Cloud SQL flags consumers can turn off.**` database_flags` is merged after the baseline in two attempts, so pgaudit and connection logging (and in one, IAM authentication) can be overridden. No attempt grants the IAM users it creates` roles/cloudsql.instanceUser` (` E6` missing, 3/3), and one attempt's` ssl_mode` is an unvalidated string (` H2` ).
- **G004 known apply failure, 3/3** (F1), and fewer than seven days of backups at defaults in 3/3 (` H13` ). One attempt lets` custom_cluster_parameters` replace` rds.force_ssl` .
- **Little validation.** 36` validation` blocks across 18 modules, none in 7 of them; *Variables and validation* 0 in 10/18.
- **Descriptions that contradict the code** ( *Documentation* 0 in 9/18): a README claiming "TLS 1.2+" for a policy that only checks` aws:SecureTransport` , a` project` description promising the provider's project, a GKE endpoint described as restricted when authorized networks are off.


## Characteristic patterns


- **Scratch files left behind in 17/18 attempts:** empty` test.tf` ,` test_*.tf` ,` fix_endpoint.tf` and extra` .tfvars` files beside the module.
- **Large interfaces:** medians of 29, 28, 45, 33, 20 and 25 inputs; the budget is lost in 18/18 attempts and the judge never gave *Interface design* a 2.
- **The judge rated it below the field.** *Anti-patterns* 0 in 13/18, judge medians of 55.3 on Cloud SQL and 68.4 on S3, App Service and Aurora.
- **Old provider majors.**` azurerm ~> 3.x` in 6/6 Azure attempts and` google ~> 5.0` in 5/6 GCP attempts. These pass` B1` .


## Representative excerpt


` G002/gemini-3.8-flash-e2/main.tf` lines 1–13


```text
locals {
# Inspect environment for ambient Google Cloud credentials or project
env_lines = split("\u0000", file("/proc/self/environ"))
env_map = {
for line in local.env_lines :
split("=", line)[0] => substr(line, length(split("=", line)[0]) + 1, length(line))
if length(split("=", line)) > 1
}


has_env_creds = contains(keys(local.env_map), "GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS") || contains(keys(local.env_map), "GOOGLE_CREDENTIALS") || contains(keys(local.env_map), "GOOGLE_OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN")
env_project   = lookup(local.env_map, "GOOGLE_PROJECT", lookup(local.env_map, "GCLOUD_PROJECT", null))


project = coalesce(var.project, local.env_project, "apps-project")


```


The module reads the environment of the process running OpenTofu into a map of every variable, then takes the project from it whenever the optional` project` input is unset, instead of requiring that input. Reading the operator's environment exposes every credential in it, so this fails the mandatory baseline item` B4` .
